Travelers stop in Toconao after trips to the high-altitude lagoons and the Atacama Salt Flat. The town portion of the route includes Saint Luke's Church and the Campanario bell tower.

A visit to the settlement replaces the open desert landscape with a walk among local buildings. Travelers then return to San Pedro de Atacama.

## Turtles, canals, and toucans: what to see in Tortuguero

Tortuguero National Park, or the "Land of Turtles," was established in 1975 and is one of Costa Rica's wildest and most biodiverse regions. Covering 26,156 hectares, it was created primarily to protect the nesting grounds of endangered sea turtles, including hawksbill, loggerhead, green, and leatherback turtles.

In Tortuguero, an extraordinary boat excursion through the canals awaits you. You can see exotic birds, flooded forests, and plants floating on the water's surface. Tortuguero's forests abound with birds, amphibians, reptiles, and mammals, including tapirs, ocelots, and river otters. There are many toucans, hawks, herons, parrots, and other birds.

As you travel along the canals, you may spot giant iguanas, lizards perched on branches, vultures circling above the treetops, and crocodiles blending into the trunks of palms. If you are there from April to May, you can see turtles laying eggs in the sand. Indeed, Tortuguero means "Land of Turtles."
